open_points.subject: Audit sequence instance mark
open_points.text: the last number written is held in the instance marks outside the store
open_points.question: What is the instance mark that owns the last audit sequence number, and which Registry actions create, advance or read it, given that State 1 says its listed models and facts are exhaustive?
options: It is a fact of a new durable instance-level model
It is a second durable representation of an AuditEntry fact
It is infrastructure state outside the Registry domain models
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an instance-level durable fact advanced atomically whenever an AuditEntry is written and read when choosing the next sequence number.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry lifecycle across restore
open_points.text: the last number written is held in the instance marks outside the store, so a restore from an older backup does not lower it
open_points.question: What happens to AuditEntries written after the restored backup, since the stated lifecycle permits an entry to disappear only through the owner's dated erasure but an older store backup would not contain them?
options: The restore may lose those entries, adding restore as another lifecycle transition
Those entries are recovered from another durable source
A backup whose restoration would lose them is refused
open_points.default_guess: Permit gaps in the restored log and treat the missing entries as lost through restore while retaining the external high-water sequence number.

open_points.subject: Migration closure instance mark
open_points.text: also held in the instance marks outside the store, which a restore does not replace
open_points.question: Does the outside-store mark hold every MigrationClosure fact—the success instant, owner principal, confirmation id and file digest—or only the fact that import has closed, and if only the latter, what MigrationClosure facts exist after restoring a pre-import backup?
options: The mark duplicates the complete MigrationClosure
The mark is only a permanent closed flag and the other facts may be absent after restore
The mark identifies another durable copy from which the complete MigrationClosure is reconstructed
open_points.default_guess: Store the complete MigrationClosure in the outside-store instance mark so the model remains present with all its required facts.

open_points.subject: Imported records after an older restore
open_points.text: absent, then present forever: a restore from an older backup does not lose it
open_points.question: If a backup from before the successful import is restored, what happens to the Projects, Customers, Rooms and ArtifactPointers created by that import while the surviving MigrationClosure still causes every further import to be refused?
options: The restore is refused unless it also contains all imported records
The imported records are recovered from another durable source
The closure is retained and the imported records remain absent
The import may be replayed despite the retained closure
open_points.default_guess: Refuse restoration of a backup that predates the successful import unless the imported records can also be recovered.

open_points.subject: Instance-level persistence boundary
open_points.text: Durable, at most one per instance; also held in the instance marks outside the store
open_points.question: How can the closure be durable outside the store when State 0 defines one instance as holding one store and State 1 enumerates MigrationClosure as Registry's durable model; are instance marks part of that store, a second Registry store, or infrastructure outside Registry?
options: Instance marks are a protected partition of the one Registry store
Instance marks are a second Registry-owned durable store
Instance marks are infrastructure state outside Registry
open_points.default_guess: Treat instance marks as a protected partition of the one Registry store with restore behavior independent of ordinary backup replacement.
